content: The mandala is an archetypal image whose occurrence is attested throughout the ages. It signifies the wholeness of the Self.
author: Carl Jung
sourceWork: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)
story:
Following his bitter break with Sigmund Freud in 1913, Swiss psychiatrist Carl Jung entered a prolonged confrontation with his own unconscious at his lakeside sanctuary in Küsnacht. Recording his visions in the famed Red Book, Jung mapped the universal archetypes, shadow instincts, and the individuation journey required to integrate one's hidden depths into psychological wholeness.

This insight points directly back to the quiet center of being. Carl Jung observed that while the mind perpetually scatters itself into past regrets and future anxieties, peace is only ever discovered by anchoring attention in the immediate truth of this moment.
reflectionPrompt: In what relationship or encounter can you practice seeing beyond outer masks into shared humanity?
